title: Practice 5: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Ты ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)) на танцы с Соней?
exercises.why: **пойдешь** is the future tense (2nd person singular) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». future: я пойду́ · ты пойдёшь · он пойдёт · мы пойдём · вы пойдёте · они пойду́т. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Will you be going to the dance with Sonya?
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: ___ (сбегать — to run there and back) в булочную за хлебом!
exercises.why: **сбегай** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **сбегать** ((colloquial) to run (to a place) and get back, to run (for), to go and get) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. imperative: сбе́гай · сбе́гайте. — Wiktionary, «сбегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «Note the preposition: after "going verbs" or the verb "to send" the preposition "за" + Instr. is used to indicate the idea of "going after" or "sending for" something or somebody: Он пошёл за газетой. — He went after the newspaper. Пошлите за доктором. — Send for the doctor.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Run and get some bread from the baker's!
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Мы ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) в ресторан.
exercises.why: **сходили** is the past tense (plural) of **сходить** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. past: он сходи́л · она сходи́ла · оно сходи́ло · они сходи́ли. — Wiktionary, «сходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Он сходил к другу.» (He went to a friend's place (and has returned; see prefixed perfective forms of motion verbs below).) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Мне надо сходить на почту за письмами.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Я хочу ___ (поездить — to ride about for a while) по Европе.
exercises.why: **поездить** (the infinitive) (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the perfective of **ездить** meaning «for a while». — Wiktionary, «поездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «a) Prefix "по-" denoting a perfective action of limited duration (an action "for a while"). The prefix "по-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: походить, поездить, полетать. These verbs denote a single completed action of limited duration, similar to the verb "погулять".» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I want to travel around Europe.
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). exercises.q: Его здоровье ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)) на убыль.
exercises.why: **пошло** is the past tense (neuter) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». past: он пошёл · она пошла́ · оно пошло́ · они пошли́. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

(Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. exercises.q: Итиро впервые ___ (поехать — to set off (by vehicle)) в Нагою.
exercises.why: **поедет** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **поехать** (to go (in a conveyance or on horseback)) — the perfective of **ехать**, «set out». future: я пое́ду · ты пое́дешь · он пое́дет · мы пое́дем · вы пое́дете · они пое́дут. — Wiktionary, «поехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The future perfective (поеду, поедешь) belongs to the 1st -е- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
